c.tagline: Where jungle ridges meet the Pacific's iron-bottom waters.

taxi.color: unmarked sedans, mostly white (no standard livery)
taxi.fareNote: Agree the fare before departing - meters aren't used. Reckon on roughly SBD 10/km within town, and SBD 100-150 for airport transfers.

emergency.medical: 111 (or go directly to National Referral Hospital, Honiara)
emergency.note: For non-urgent medical advice some residents call 713 6000; mobile coverage can be patchy so know your location/landmark before calling.

hood_landmark.Panatina: University of the South Pacific Solomon Islands Campus, Panatina

avoid.reason: Occasional unrest/riots (Chinatown targeted in the past) and petty crime; caution at night

hood_desc: The compact downtown core along Mendana Avenue with the port, government offices, high commissions and the city's flagship waterfront hotels; ideal for business travelers and anyone wanting everything walkable.
Honiara's original commercial heart around the bustling Central Market and Chinese-run trade stores; a lively, budget-friendly base close to minibus routes and local life.
An eastern strip of shops, the National Referral Hospital and casino nightlife along Kukum Highway; suits longer-stay visitors wanting a quieter, more residential feel just outside the CBD.
A leafy hillside residential area near the National Museum and botanical gardens, home to embassy staff and NGO workers; good for travelers wanting calm surroundings a short drive from town.
An eastern suburb near the university campus and closer to Henderson Airport; convenient for early flights, conferences and trips to the eastern side of Guadalcanal.
lodging: St Agnes Mothers Union Rest House

water.note: Chlorinated piped water has improved in recent years, but bottled or boiled water is still the safer bet for visitors.

sys.n: Open-backed truck buses (where minibus routes don't reach)

transit.pay: Pay cash directly to the driver or conductor when boarding or alighting; fares are flat within central zones (about SBD 3) and rise slightly for longer routes. There is no rechargeable card or app-based payment system.
transit.hours: Minibuses run roughly 6am-7pm with no fixed timetable; there is no scheduled night service, so pre-arranged taxis are used after dark.
transit.note: Honiara has no formal bus routes - PMV minibuses depart from the Central Market hub when full and can be flagged down anywhere along their route.

bus: PMV minibuses linking Central Market to Kukum, White River, Tanaghai and Panatina/Henderson

airport.name: Honiara International Airport (HIR)
rentals: No major international rental chains operate at the airport; a handful of local operators arrange car hire, usually through hotels

tip.r: Tipping isn't part of local Melanesian custom, though hotel and resort staff may appreciate a small tip for good service.

landmarks: Vilu War Museum
An open-air museum displaying WWII wreckage—downed planes, tanks, and artillery—scattered among jungle foliage, a haunting reminder of the Guadalcanal Campaign.
Bloody Ridge (Edson's Ridge)
The site of a pivotal 1942 WWII battle overlooking Honiara, now a quiet memorial ridge with sweeping views and monuments to the fallen.
Guadalcanal American Memorial
A hilltop monument honoring US forces who fought in the Guadalcanal Campaign, offering panoramic views over Honiara and Iron Bottom Sound.
Point Cruz
Honiara's historic waterfront harbor area, the bustling heart of the capital where markets, wharves, and city life meet the sea.
Honiara Central Market
A vibrant, colorful market bursting with tropical produce and handicrafts, offering an authentic slice of daily Solomon Islands life.
National Museum of Solomon Islands
A small but rich museum showcasing traditional Melanesian art, shell money, war canoes, and WWII relics from across the archipelago.
Iron Bottom Sound
The strait off Honiara's coast named for the dozens of WWII warships and planes sunk beneath its waters, now a renowned wreck-diving site.
Solomon Peace Memorial Park (Mount Austen)
A Japanese-built peace memorial atop Mount Austen with commanding views over Honiara and the coastline where fierce WWII fighting once raged.
Betikama War Relics Museum
A missionary-run museum near Honiara displaying an eclectic collection of WWII aircraft wreckage and military artifacts alongside local carvings.
Parliament House, Honiara
The distinctive circular, thatched-roof-inspired national parliament building, a striking symbol of Solomon Islands' modern identity.

train.note: The Solomon Islands has no railways of any kind. Getting around Honiara is by shared minibus; travel to other islands is by boat or by Solomon Airlines domestic flights.

bus.note: Honiara is on Guadalcanal, an island nation, so there are no international coach routes. Local transport is cheap shared minibuses along the main Honiara road; there is no long-distance intercity bus network.

ferry.note: No scheduled international passenger ferries. Domestic inter-island ships leave from Honiara's main wharf to Auki (Malaita), Tulagi (Central) and Gizo (Western Province via Marovo); operators include Pelican Shipping, Fair West Shipping, Franjti Shipping and Marina Shipping. Most have no online booking - timetables are posted at the wharf and Honiara Yacht Club, so ask locally and book in person.

half.name: Savo Island
half.blurb: Volcanic island reached by boat, with megapode nesting fields, hot springs, and a crater hike.

half.name: Bonegi Beach
half.blurb: Black-sand beach with WWII shipwrecks visible just offshore, popular for snorkeling and diving.

half.name: Mataniko Falls
half.blurb: Waterfall reached by a jungle trail east of the city, with a swimmable pool at its base.

full.name: Tulagi
full.blurb: Former colonial capital in the Florida Islands, with WWII wreck-diving sites in Ironbottom Sound.
